maya (runtime): Heads up — after yesterday's kernel selector change EU p99 latency climbed ~120ms, p95 ~40ms. US looks fine. Suspect kernel fallthrough -> CPU fallback + cross-zone spillover. :eyes:

maya (runtime): Quick stats from the spike window (sample):
```
[2026-03-14T22:03:10Z] req_id=ea3f region=eu kernel=opt_v2 fallback=cpu latency_ms=842
kernel_select: opt_v2 -> fallback_cpu: 56% of slow samples
batch_size=6 token_budget=128 queue_len=18
KV-cache: hit_rate=0.82 miss_rate=0.18 warmup_seconds=3.4
```

sophia (ml): Hmm. KV warmup in EU looks worse (higher miss-rate) which will push more work to the slow path and trigger kernel fallback. Also lots of small batches (batch_size median 4) so we lose throughput efficiency.

dan (infra): Do we have flamegraphs / perf traces for the kernel path vs fallback? Can we prove cross-zone egress is happening?

maya (runtime): Pasted small sample flame + traces to the thread — top stack shows kernel_select -> dispatch_to_remote -> wait_for_remote_slot in many samples. That matches cross-zone handoff. :mag:

alex (eng): Proposal for a controlled experiment (EU only):
- increase token_budget_target from 128 -> 256 for region=eu
- increase batch_window from 50ms -> 80ms (more time to form bigger batches)
- enable eager KV prefetch for region=eu (KV warmup aggressive)
- prefer same-zone capacity in routing policy even if kernel mismatch (soft affinity)
Rollout: canary 10% users -> monitor 24h -> scale to 50% if metrics good. :rocket:

sophia (ml): Sounds good. Also add a metric for effective KV hit-rate by seq_len bucket. That will tell us if prefetch helps long-seq requests.

maya (runtime): Config snippet for canary (eu 10%):
```
region: eu
canary: 0.10
kernel_selector:
  prefer_same_zone: true
batching:
  token_budget_target: 256
  batch_window_ms: 80
kv_cache:
  eager_prefetch: true
```

perf-bot: [alert] microbench: opt_v2 kernel shows +8% p99 regression for seq=1024 vs baseline (timestamp=1765432200). See CI run #3421.

dan (infra): Noted. We'll correlate microbench regression with production traces. If opt_v2 regressed, prefer fallback to older kernel version in EU until root cause fixed.

maya (runtime): Action items:
1) run canary with alex's config tomorrow 09:00 UTC (eu 10%)
2) sophia to collect KV hit-rate by seq_len and flamegraphs for slow traces
3) dan to check cross-zone egress delta and cost impact
4) perf-bot to post CI/perf signals to this thread

maya (runtime): tagging @sophia (ml) @dan (infra) @alex (eng) — will start canary and report. :thumbsup:

sophia (ml): ack. will upload flamegraphs and a small dashboard for kv-hit vs latency. :eyes:

dan (infra): I'll also add a temporary routing rule to bias same-zone locality for EU canary. If we see increased cost, rollback.

perf-bot: deploy started: eu-canary-10pct at ts=1765432500. CI perf alerts will update here.

maya (runtime): thanks — will monitor p50/p95/p99, spillover_ratio, kv_hit, cost/unit. Back with numbers after 1h.

alex (eng): Also consider gating kernel swap by batch-size distribution: if median batch_size < 5, don't switch to opt_v2 in that region. Could avoid mismatches.

maya (runtime): Good idea. Adding as follow-up if canary still noisy.

maya (runtime): TL;DR: kernel selector change seems to interact poorly with KV warmup and batching in EU -> cross-zone spillover. Running eu-only canary with larger token_budget + longer batch window + eager-kv + soft same-zone affinity. Monitor metrics, flamegraphs, and CI signals.
